title: Smart Cursor toggle
player_outcome: Pressing X toggles Smart Cursor, and the crosshair turns orange with a small icon. With a pickaxe it snaps to the nearest block you can actually mine near your aim within reach; with an axe, to the nearest tree. Mining an ore vein or chopping a forest stops needing pixel-perfect aim.
design:
Core: new src/Strata.Core/Gameplay/Interaction/SmartTargeting.cs. Targeting is a non-partial static class, so this is a separate class.
- `Target? Find(VoxelWorld world, Vector3 eye, Vector3 aim, float reachM, ItemUseInfo info, int pickPower, int axePower, int hammerPower)`.
- Mine: march the ray in 0.25 m steps; at each step test cells within lateral radius min(0.75 m, dist·tan 12°) for solid blocks where MiningRules.CanMine(block, pickPower). Return the one closest along the ray.
- Chop/Hammer: the nearest TileObject within the cone that the tool can break.
- Otherwise null, and the plain target is used.

Input: add "smart_cursor": ["key:X"] to input.json (Ctrl is already crouch). Add it to KeyBindings.Listed.
- `UserSettings.SmartCursor` persists the toggle.
- The Gameplay settings row gets 'Smart cursor'.

InteractionController (after P1's eye-ray targeting lands): when SmartCursor is on and the held item has Mine, Chop or Hammer, replace Target with SmartTargeting.Find and set InReach = true. The toggle writes 'Smart Cursor On'/'Off' to the StatusLine. Hud Crosshair tints orange and shows the smart_cursor sprite. TargetHighlight already follows Interaction.Target.
files_modify: game/Player/InteractionController.cs — smart target branch and toggle
tests: SmartTargetingTests: FindsOreBesideTheRay (ore cell 0.5 m off-axis); IgnoresBlocksTooHardForThePick; ChopsNearestTreeInCone; NothingBeyondReach
ui.cmds: `press smart_cursor` / `press smart_cursor off` / `assert ui.smart_cursor == 1` / `wield copper_pickaxe` / `aim 0.3 -1 0.1` / `hold use_primary 1.5` / `assert inv.stone >= 1`
verification: dotnet test; headless smoke; manual mining in a cave with Smart Cursor on
risks: Depends on P1's targeting rewrite (the ray from the eye and entity picking, section G). Schedule after P1's targeting WP to avoid double-editing UpdateTarget.
Performance: the cone search is bounded (at most ~40 steps × 9 cells); run it only when the held tool or aim changes by more than 0.5°.
